brief: Evercore ISI's morning note leads with Jensen Huang's reinstatement as NVDA CEO, framed as backed by the Trump administration: the firm argues this shows the U.S. government has become the implicit backstop of the AI industrial complex, calling it AI's first bailout of the buildout's financing architecture rather than a balance sheet, with implications for capital allocation and risk premiums on AI infrastructure financing. The rest of the note is a roundup of single-name calls (NFLX, Bloom Energy, PayPal, Adyen, Apple, RingCentral, ADI, Sensata, FUBO, SanDisk, SpaceX) alongside three recurring debates: whether AI infrastructure stocks can capture the economic value AI creates given token-price deflation and a delayed free-cash-flow recovery, even as NVDA posts a record $20B Vera Rubin ramp, a $2.5T cloud backlog and guides 75% FY28 revenue growth while the SOX multiple compresses late-cycle; cybersecurity demand (CRWD, OKTA, PANW, SNOW) strengthening into CY27; and memory costs pressuring Apple's margins while driving SanDisk's post-split earnings beat.
